School counsellor's note, Class 11. Written by Himani, 3 September.
Pritam came to see me today, sent by his class teacher because he has looked exhausted for weeks. He told me he hates the computer science tuition he has attended for two years, three evenings a week. He says he would rather put that time into art, where he is doing well. When I asked why he continues, he said, "My mother, Sarita aunty, already paid for this year. And I've done two years. If I stop now, what was it for?" He said it looked like a reason, but he seemed trapped by it. I asked him what the next two years would look like if he kept going, and he went quiet. We made a plan: he will write down what he'd do with those three evenings, and I will meet him and his mother together next Tuesday.

Your nephew,
Kamal

When I was fifteen, my parents enrolled me in a medical entrance coaching institute in Kottayam. The fees were huge for our family. By the second year, I knew I hated biology. I wanted to study architecture. I sketched buildings in the margins of my notes.

But every time I thought of quitting, I saw my father counting notes for the fees. Two years. All that money. How could I waste it?

So I stayed another year. I failed the entrance, of course. Then I finally told my father.

I did architecture after that. So, Ojas, what do you want the next year to be for?

Now he was fifteen and hated it. He wanted to spend his evenings at the robotics club.

"If you keep going just because of the past," Damini said, "you'll lose the robotics club too."

Kiran was quiet all the way to class. That night, he asked Amma if they could talk after dinner.
